subject: Biologi
title: Genetics and heredity
sourceSummary: DNA, genes and chromosomes, dominant and recessive inheritance, and how to read a Punnett square to calculate probabilities.

questions.opener: Think about what is found in the cell nucleus and carries the information for how you are built.
choices: A substance that stores and carries genetic information
A type of sugar that gives the cell energy
questions.explanation: DNA is the genetic material — a long molecule that contains the instructions (genes) for how an organism is built and functions. It is not a protein, a membrane, or an energy source in itself.

questions.opener: Think of DNA as a recipe book — what then corresponds to a single recipe?
choices: A section of DNA that carries information about a particular trait
A protein that breaks down food
questions.explanation: A gene is a piece of the DNA molecule that contains information about a specific trait, such as eye colour. A chromosome consists of many genes packed together.

questions.prompt: Where in the cell are the chromosomes found?
questions.opener: Where is DNA stored in the cell?
questions.explanation: The chromosomes, which are tightly packed DNA, are found in the cell nucleus. Humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs) in almost all of their cells.

questions.prompt: If the allele for brown eyes (B) is dominant over the allele for blue eyes (b), what eye colour does a person with the allele pair Bb have?
questions.opener: With dominant/recessive inheritance, one dominant allele is enough for the trait to show.
choices: Both blue and brown at the same time
questions.explanation: Because B (brown eyes) is dominant, one B allele is enough for the trait to show, even if the person also carries b. Only someone with bb (two recessive alleles) has blue eyes.

questions.opener: Think about what can happen when DNA is copied or damaged.
choices: A normal cell division without any change
A sudden change in the DNA
A process where two cells merge together
questions.explanation: A mutation is a change in the DNA sequence, which can arise by mistake during copying or due to external influences such as radiation. Mutations can be harmful, neutral, or sometimes beneficial.

questions.prompt: Two people who are both Bb (B = brown eyes, dominant; b = blue eyes, recessive) have a child. What is the probability that the child has blue eyes (bb)?
questions.opener: Draw a Punnett square with Bb x Bb and count how many of the four boxes are bb.
questions.explanation: The Punnett square for Bb x Bb gives the combinations BB, Bb, Bb, bb — so 1 of 4 (25%) is bb and has blue eyes. The other 3 of 4 have brown eyes because B is dominant.

questions.prompt: Two pea plants, both with the allele pair Tt (T = tall, dominant; t = short, recessive), are crossed. Draw a Punnett square and calculate what proportion of the offspring will be short plants.
questions.opener: Set up a 2x2 grid with the parents' gametes (T and t) along the sides and fill in the combinations.
questions.answer: 25% (1 of 4) will be short plants (tt). 75% will be tall (TT or Tt).
steps: Each parent is Tt and produces gametes with either T or t.
Set up a grid with T and t from one parent across the top, and T and t from the other parent down the side.
Fill in the four boxes: TT, Tt, Tt, tt.
TT and Tt (3 of 4) become tall plants because T is dominant, tt (1 of 4) becomes short because both alleles are recessive.
The probability of a short plant is therefore 25%.

questions.prompt: Summarise the basic concepts in genetics: DNA, gene, chromosome, dominant and recessive.
questions.opener: Go through the concepts in order of size, from smallest to largest.
questions.answer: DNA: the molecule that carries all genetic information, found in the cell nucleus · Gene: a section of DNA with information about a particular trait · Chromosome: tightly packed DNA, humans have 46 of them (23 pairs) · Dominant allele: shows even if the person has only one copy of it (written with a capital letter, e.g. B) · Recessive allele: only shows if the person has two copies of it (written with a lowercase letter, e.g. b) · Mutation: a change in DNA that can produce new traits and is a basis for variation and evolution.
